newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Protest dog void of poll re-run in Nigeria capital.
newsitem.headline: Protest dog void of poll re-run in Nigeria capital.

text.p: Candidates of four of Nigeria's five political parties on Thursday protested against an official decision not to repeat municipal polls in the capital Abuja.
The electoral commission (NECON) had listed three municipal areas in Abuja were among 139 areas out of the nation's 774 where it said the March 15 polls were inconclusive and should be held again.
But NECON cancelled that decision after Lieutenant-General Jeremiah Useni, the minister of the federal capital territory Abuja, said there was no need for it.
"We condemn the visible interference and outright disregard of the electoral guidelines by the Federal Capital Authority," said a statement signed by the candidates and given to the media.
Useni, one of Nigeria's most powerful generals, has already sworn in councillors elected for Abuja, saying NECON had told him there was no problem with the earlier vote in the capital.
The candidates said in the statement that their opponents who Useni swore in to office on March 24 were not duly elected.
NECON spokesman Steve Osemeke said the commission called off the re-run in order to probe the claims of the candidates.

Local radio stations reported that voter turn-out was light in the repeat polls on Thursday and in the southeastern Cross River state it was delayed to Friday because of the late arrival of voting materials.
The council polls are the first on a partisan basis under a programme the Nigerian military government says will restore democracy next year.
A previous attempt at transition to civil rule ended in a fiasco in 1993 when a presidential vote was annulled, plunging the populous African nation into chaos.

A majority of the councils in the recent poll were won by two parties that have said they would like to adopt General Abacha, who seized power in the chaos of 1993, as their candidate in next year's presidential poll.
